Commentary.Commentary: That's all we have from this one-sided affair. Let's hope for a better contest in the second ODI at Trent Bridge on 21st September at 1230 local (1130 GMT). Until then, it's goodbye and cheers!

Man of the Match, Jonny Bairstow says it wasn't a great time to slip but was delighted to come back for the third run for his ton. Admits that it seems a long time ago since he made his ODI debut so he wants to make the most of the opportunity given to him. Ends by saying the internal competition in the team helps everyone to become better and do more.

Eoin Morgan says he thought they came back well. Continues saying West Indies started off well but his team adapted to the conditions quickly. Adds their bowling was great according to him which kept the target to a decent amount. On the dropped chance, mentions Root doesn't drop many so it's important to keep creating chances. Praises Rashid as he kept bowling well, as did the bowling unit in general which was very encouraging to see. When asked about Bairstow, states that after a performance like this, it's very difficult to leave him out.

Jason Holder reckons they were 40 runs short. Admits they didn't bowl well and conceded too many boundaries. Realizes that his side needs to rotate strike if the boundaries are not coming, that it's an area of concern. Acknowledges the contrast from T20 cricket. Adds they lost wickets at crucial moments and let themselves down by being too inconsistent. When asked about missing out on automatic World Cup qualification, says there's work to be done obviously, but the focus is on this series with Trent Bridge coming up first.

West Indies were of no match. Apart from Chris Gayle's onslaught at the beginning, they never were in the game. Their bowlers were anything but impressive and it turned out to be a no contest. Courtesy this loss, the visitors now will have to play the World Cup qualifiers next year. Their tussle with Sri Lanka ends here and the Islanders will be thankful to England.

Comfortable win for England. They were after a mediocre target and achieved it with minimum fuss. Jonny Bairstow and Alex Hales gave a quick start before the century stand for the second wicket almost sealed the deal. Bairstow grabbed the opportunity to open the innings with both hands and scored an unbeaten century to see his side through.
SIX! Finishes it in one blow. Tossed up ball, Stokes gets underneath it after dancing down the track and dismisses it over long on for a maximum. England win by 7 wickets!
Flatter delivery on middle, worked through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.

Maiden ODI hundred for Jonny Bairstow! Big moment for him. The crowd is on its feet and the English players in the balcony are applauding his effort. Flighted delivery, full and outside off, Jonny advances down the track and drills it through covers. Slips a bit while turning for the third run but completes the run with ease. He is all pumped up. Superb knock and Bairstow will be thrilled to grab this opportunity to open the innings.
Turning back into the batsman from a shorter length outside off, Jonny goes back and punches it to covers.
Flighted and full outside off, forced straight to covers.
SIX! High and handsome! Angling away from the batsman, Stokes dances down the track and launches it over long off for a biggie. 13 from the over!
Goes short and outside off, Bairstow plays the ramp shot and it's on one bounce to the third man fielder. A single taken.
Full in length and around off, Stokes bunts it to mid off and scampers across to the other end. The fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end and it hits Ben in the process. No harm done.
Good length ball on middle and leg, it's turned in front of square leg for a single.
FOUR! Good timing! Slower delivery, full and outside off, Bairstow strokes it square of the wicket on the off side and finds the fence in spite of the diving effort in the deep.
An off cutter outside off, punched to short cover.
Knocks a full ball down to long on for one.
Presses forward and helps it off the inside half of the bat through the leg side for a run.
Stokes has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Goes back and pushes it back to the bowler.
Driven towards the mid on region. They pick up a single.
Full and flighted outside off, driven straight to mid off.
FOUR! Well played! A full toss outside off, Stokes walks across the stumps and punches it back. It goes wide of the bowler and races past mid on for a boundary.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They manage to come back for the second.s.
Slower again, full and around off, Jonny plays it across the line this time, towards mid on and steals a single.
Slower and fuller, around off, Jonny pushes it to covers.

Edged but safe. Kesrick Williams is amidst terrific rhythm at the moment. Gets one to skid away from the new batsman, Stokes plays at it away from his body and edges it through the vacant gully region for a run. Off the mark in a streaky manner.
Ben Stokes walks in next.

OUT! Gone, caught behind! Zippy delivery, a touch short and around off, skidding off the surface, Morgan pushes inside the line, maybe trying to play it late but it takes the outside edge and settles safely into the gloves of the keeper. All too late for the Windies. 30 more needed off 89 balls.
Quicker delivery, outside off and skidding off the surface, Jonny pushes at it and misses.
Tossed up ball on middle, flicked to mid-wicket.
Terrific delivery, full and outside off, drifting away, Jonny tries to drive but it skids through the surface to beat the bat.
Full flighted on off, a little lap sweep played by Bairstow to fine leg for a couple of runs.
Again it's flatter through the air and lands full around off, Bairstow plays it out from the crease to the on side.
Flatter and shorter from around the wicket, it's outside off and Morgan cuts it through point for a single.
Ashley Nurse is back on.

A little short in length on middle, shaping away a touch, Morgan tries defending from the back foot but is squared up in the process. He ends up playing it off the outside edge and it rolls to the left of Gayle at wide first slip. They pick up a single.
Length ball on off, Bairstow taps it down to point and takes off for a quick single.
Digs in a short ball on off, Jonny drops his wrists and allows it through to the keeper.
Edgy! Short in length and outside off, Morgan pushes inside the line and edges it down to third man for a run.
Short in length and outside off, Bairstow slaps it through covers and takes three runs. This is now Jonny's highest ODI score.
Back of a length ball on off, Morgan stays back and just deflects it down to third man for a run.
Full and angling in on middle, Bairstow gets behind the line and defends it to mid on.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Great placement. The follow-up delivery by Jerome is a well-cooked up fullish ball outside off, Morgan threads the gap between extra cover and mid off for a boundary.
Wide called for height. The bouncer from Taylor goes wrong, well over Morgan's head who ducks.
Fullish and on off, driven off the front foot after a trademark-crouching-trigger-movement by Morgan. Straight to the cover fielder.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
A proper slip in place.
Good length delivery around off, Morgan tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Slower delivery, an off cutter around middle, Bairstow nudges it down to fine leg and collects a couple of runs.
Sliding down the leg side, on a shortish length, Morgan tucks it down to fine leg for  a single.
Skipper Eoin Morgan arrives. A wide first slip in place.

OUT! Drags it on. Williams gets a wicket against the run of play. A wicket too late for the Windies. Back of a length ball on off, angling in and cramping the batsman for room. Joe tries to play late from the crease, maybe attempting to run it down to third man but ends up dragging it onto the stumps. It also brings the curtain down on the century partnership. 49 more needed for a win!
Bouncer outside off, quite high, Root allows it through and it's called a wide.
Stays back to a length ball and strokes it through covers for two runs.
Goes wide of the crease and angles in a length ball on off, Bairstow pushes it from the crease to covers for a run.
Shortish and on off, Bairstow plays it down with an angled bat to short third man.
Kesrick Williams is brought back into the attack.
Played to the point region by the batsman. No run.
Goes on the back foot and punches it through covers for a couple of runs. The fielder in the deep has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Could have been close in case of a direct hit.
23rd ODI fifty for Joe Root, surely one of his easiest. A short delivery again and Joe plays a pull shot through square leg for a couple of runs. The run-machine continues to deliver for England.
Digs in a short ball around off, Root does well to keep his pull shot down and it races through square leg. They take a couple of runs.
A little short in length around off, Root plays a short-arm jab but finds short mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery around off, Root goes on his toes and pats it down to backward point.
Drinks break.
FOUR! Given up, it seems. Bishoo continues to be on the shorter side and this time it's clobbered down past the bowler for a boundary. 15 from the over, 59 needed from 120 balls.
FOUR! Bishoo dishes out yet another half-tracker in this over, Bairstow shows no mercy and crunches it through covers for a boundary.
Again a short ball and it has been cut straight to the point fielder.
Rocks back to a short ball and punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
FOUR! A long hop by Bishoo, around middle, Root eases himself deep inside the crease and pulls it past wide mid on for a boundary.
Shoddy fielding. Short and just outside off, Root gets back and plays a late cut. The point fielder allows it through him and they take a brace.
Good yorker around middle, Jonny digs it back to the bowler.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
Pitches it full and outside off, Jonny drives but finds mid off.
FOUR! The 100-run stand comes up. A short of a length delivery outside off has been whacked through point for a cracking boundary.
Fetches a short ball from outside off and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
A touch short and around off, Root stays back and taps it down to backward point.
Jerome Taylor is back on.
Flighted full outside off, driven to sweeper cover for one.
Kneels and sweeps it behind square leg for a run.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Goes on the back foot and punches it through covers for a single.

FOUR! Jonny, Jonny - Yes papa! Hitting boundaries - Yes papa! Loving the bowling - Yes papa! What are Windies' chances - Ha..ha..ha! A late cut this time to the shorter delivery, beats first slip and it races away to the the third man fence. England cruising.
FOUR! Poor length, Bishoo gets it to turn away but it's on the shorter side. Bairstow gets deep inside the crease and hammers it past mid on for a boundary.
A run off every ball, the scoreboard keeps ticking. Tapped in front of point by JB for a quick single.
Eases it down to long on for one.
Works it away with the spin on the leg side. No run taken.
Flatter delivery, punched just wide of the bowler who manages a half-stop towards mid-wicket.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They manage to come back for the second.
Full in length outside off, driven through the covers for a couple of runs.

Not out! Lovely loopy delivery from Bishoo, on off. It spins away and beats Bairstow who looks to slog it across the line. Is slightly off balance and so Hope takes the bails off. Appeals for a stumping and it's taken upstairs. Replays show that Jonny makes it back in time. He's safe.
Stumping appeal is taken upstairs...
Stays back to keep it out off the back foot.
The batsman plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man.
Plays with the spin again and pushes it towards cover-point. Single taken.
Straighter one from Bishoo, Bairstow goes deep in the crease and whips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Landed on a driving length, spinning away from around off, Bairstow chases after it only to get beaten.
Short again, on the stumps, punched off the back foot to long on for a single.
Quick outside off, punched past cover for a run.
Waits for the ball to come to him, opens the face and guides to short third man.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Manages to connect the paddle this time. Beats the keeper and picks up two.
Spinning down the leg side, Root looks to paddle but fails to connect. The keeper misses it as well and so, the batsmen take a run. Wide signalled by the umpire.
Flatter trajectory, punched to the right of the bowler.
Spinning away, Jonny opens the face to push it with the turn but misses.

FOUR! 6th ODI fifty for Jonny Bairstow! Lovely knock, he walks over to his Test skipper and celebrates with a solid handshake. Can easily tell he's waited a long time for this, is making the most of the opportunity now. Backs away and finds the deep backward point fence with a fierce cut to reach the milestone.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Outside off, kneels down to sweep but misses.
Better. Draws Bairstow forward, beats him in the flight and the turn, almost taking the outside edge.
Still quite wayward with his lengths. It's a bit short and is lucky Root doesn't punish him. The cut finds the cover fielder.
Pushed quicker through the air on off, blocked from deep inside the crease.
Knocks it down the ground, towards long on and takes a single.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Another one shorter in length, a punch is given in response as it's hit to mid on.
Quicker delivery outside off, cut to the man at cover.
Off spinner on off, turning in, JB goes back and off the inner half plays it to short mid-wicket.
Kept a bit low. Skid off the surface too but Bairstow did well. Cut it away through cover-point to retain strike.
Camps back and meets the skidding ball with the full face of the bat.
Dropped short, Bairstow slaps it to sweeper cover and runs hard to be able to come back for the second.
Spinning away on a full length from outside off, Joe comes ahead and pushes it by leaning into the shot. Into the gap in the covers and a single is taken.
FOUR! That's a wonderful shot! Full outside off, Root drags the slog sweep beautifully and hammers it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Very Kevin Pietersen-esque from Joe, very well executed.
Short and wide, cut hard straight to the man at point.
Straighter one skidding off the surface outside off, looks to cut it away but is beaten by pace.
Floats it up around off, Jonny is forward in defense.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Knocks this full ball down to long off and takes one.
Gripping off the surface and spinning in rather sharply, Bairstow somehow manages to get some bat on it. An inside edge which then thuds him on the pads.
Tossed up and spinning in on middle and leg, Bairstow is down on his rear knee to sweep but is hit on the pads.
Eases this full ball down to long off and ends the over with a comfortable single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The 50-run stand is up in no time. These two have motored along pretty nicely here. Bairstow hits it a bit square through point and comes back for the second.
Landed short again, outside off, punched to the covers.
Similar shot from Jonny Bairstow. He offers a decent punch through the covers and gets a couple to his name.
Spinning away from around off, dropped a little shorter in length, Root goes back to punch it through to sweeper cover for a run.
Devendra Bishoo is brought on to have a go with the ball.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Straighter one outside off, blocked solidly off the front foot.
On middle and leg on a fuller length, swept down to fine leg. One more taken.
Flicks it with fast hands through the mid-wicket region for a single.
Floats it up on middle and off, wristed down comfortably to long on to rotate strike.

FOUR! Clever from Root, that's very well done. Full toss outside off, he kneels down and plays the reverse paddle by taking it on the full. No slip in place and so, the ball races away to the third man boundary.
Short of a length ball which Root drops it in front of backward point with soft hands. Brisk single taken.
Takes the pace off this one, Bairstow however picks it up and flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Short of a good length, pulled away in front of square on the leg side for a single.

Moving into the batsman a little late, almost takes Jonny Bairstow by surprise. He goes for the expansive drive and ends up getting an inside edge back onto his pads. Root is alert to the situation and quickly calls his partner through for a run.
Sloppy from the West Indies captain. Root pushes it towards him at mid off and he fumbles. It allows the batsmen to cross over for a single.
Fuller length ball on the pads, flicked through to deep square leg for a run.
Powerplay 2 has been signalled. 4 fielders will now be allowed outside the 30-yard circle.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and straight from Nurse, Root with an easy drive to mid on for a single.
Picks it off his pads and flicks it into the leg side for another one.
Hangs back as this is flat and short, kept out off the back foot.
FOUR! Tossed up this time and Bairstow puts it away with ease. Leans into it and drives it sweetly through the gap in the covers for a boundary.
Half-tracker to begin proceedings, outside off, Jonny backs away and smacks it straight to the cover fielder.
Ashley Nurse is introduced into the bowling attack.
Bit slower in pace, worked away on the leg side. One run taken.
On the shorter side of the length, lobbed down towards third man for a double.
FOUR! Poor line. Down the leg side, just needed a tickle and that's what Jonny Bairstow's done. Flicks it fine down the leg side, across the fine leg fence for a boundary.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Spears in a full delivery just outside off, Root drives but finds the man at mid off.
Back of a length around off, dabs it with an open face through gully for a run.
Kesrick Williams to bowl.
Works it through mid-wicket and ends the over with a single.
Picks it off his pads and flicks it into the leg side for a single.
FOUR! Short ball on off, Root moves inside the line and plays the pull shot. Clears short fine leg, just about, but does clear it. Picks up a boundary as the ball races to the fence.
Stays back and keeps it out off the back foot.
Short in length again, pulled away to deep mid-wicket once more, but for just a single this time.
Short of a good length around off, Bairstow rocks onto his back foot and short-arm jabs it over mid-wicket. A fumble from the man in the deep allows the batsmen to easily come back for the second.
Good length ball seaming away late, Jonny plays it late as he guides it to the third man fielder for a run.
Played to the point region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Slanting in on middle and leg, on a full length, Jonny Bairstow works it wide of mid on and scampers through.

That was dangerous! Root drops it to the left of the bowler and sets off. Holder gets to the ball and has a shy at the bowler's end after turning. Just misses but had he hit, Joe would have been gone.
Outside off with some room to work with, Bairstow opens the face and runs it down to third man for a single.
Shaping back in on middle, clipped through mid-wicket by Root for one.
Nicely done. Works it down in front of mid-wicket with soft hands and calls his partner through for a quick single.
Goes full, attacks the stumps, driven straight to mid on.
Pegs Root back again with another shortish delivery. The English run-machine defends it right under his nose this time.
Shortish around off, Root with soft hands taps it down on the off side.
Joe Root walks in at No.3.

OUT! West Indies needed an early breakthrough and they've got it. Alex Hales is gone! Back of a length on off, Hales makes a little room and cuts hard. Can't keep it down and it flies straight into the hands of Evin Lewis at point. He fumbles at first but then takes it comfortably on the second attempt. Can the Windies snatch a couple of more wickets quickly to get back in the game?
FOUR! EXQUISITE! He likes the pace, doesn't he? It's full and in the slot, Alex Hales with the full face of the bat drives it straight back past the bowler for a boundary.
Good length delivery outside off, Bairstow pushes at it and gets it away from the bottom half. It goes towards the first slip fielder on a couple of bounces.
Lands it on a length outside off, there is width on offer, Jonny hits through the line but finds the cover-point fielder.

FOUR! Slower delivery, a miscued shot but still a boundary. Fullish and angling in from outside off, Bairstow mistimes his attempted shot, the bottom hand comes off the handle and it balloons over mid on for a boundary.
On the pads again, it's clipped quietly to mid-wicket for a single.
Fullish and on middle and leg, it's pushed down the ground but straight to mid on.
Wrong line, full and going down the leg side, Bairstow flicks it through backward square leg for a single.
Hits the yorker mark around off, Hales digs it out to the off side.
Fuller in length and on middle, Hales flicks it through mid-wicket and takes a couple of runs.
Play and a miss! A nothing shot by Alex. A touch short in length and outside off, Hales tries playing it late from the crease but misses.
Mid-wicket drops back.

FOUR! On one bounce to the fence. Hales is looking in great touch, picking length in a trice. Taylor bangs it short around off and Alex is already waiting for it on the back foot. Pulls it with utter disdain over mid-wicket and collects another boundary.
Back of a length ball on off, once again Hales tries to punch it from the crease. However, this time it comes from the outside half of the bat and goes to point.
A touch short and on off, Hales with a back foot punch finds the cover-point fielder.
Outside off, left alone. England off to a decent start.

FOUR! Nicely timed and in the gap! A length delivery in the region outside off, Bairstow presses forward and creams his drive through extra cover. The mid off fielder is quick but not quick enough to prevent the boundary.
Taps a length ball to point and looks for a run. He is sent back.
Good length delivery close to the off stump line, Jonny pushes inside the line with soft hands and gets it past the slip cordon off the outside edge. It runs down to third man and they cross.
Too full in length on this occasion, Bairstow reaches out and squeezes it out to cover-point.
Hurls a length delivery in the channel outside off, Bairstow shoulders arms.
Jason Holder to operate from the other end.
Back of a length delivery on off, Hales rocks back and punches it with great force to covers. Finds the fielder though.

FOUR! Sloppy by Mohammed! Taylor errs in line this time, angling down the leg side, Hales picks it off his pads and flicks it through the gap at mid-wicket. Mohammed gives the chase from mid on, puts in a dive near the fence and tries to flick it back. But he ends up flicking it over the rope.
FOUR! Hales is away in style. Dominates the short ball quite well. He is on top of the bounce and dismisses it with a murderous pull shot to the deep mid-wicket fence.
Serves it on a length one more time, around off, Hales gets behind the line and blocks it back.
Good length again, around off, Jonny keeps it out behind square leg and gets off the mark with a single. England are away!
Starts with a length delivery just around off, holding its line, Bairstow watches the line closely before making the leave.

Time for the chase! Alex Hales is out in the middle with his new opening partner, Jonny Bairstow. 205 needed off 252 legal balls. Jerome Taylor to steam in with the first new ball. A couple of slips in place. Early wickets will be the key if the Windies want to stay in hunt. Here we go...
